text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A repackaged Social Democratic Party is relaunched with much fanfare amid warnings by officials it will not be a "safety net" for political rejects.
- Finance Minister Musalia Mudavadi launches venture capital facility initially capitalised at one billion shillings.

- In a move seen as a break from his previous rejectionist stance, opposition FORD-Asili Chairman Kenneth Matiba says he isprepared to meet other opposition chiefs to plan strategy for the general election.
- Cornered gangsters use screaming, frightened schoolchildren as human shields to ward off police bullets.
- Business in parliament is interrupted for two minutes as Internal Security Minister Jackson Kalweo is nearly punched by a fellow member of parliament Peter Leshore.
- The doctor-in-charge at a mission hospital says the rape of minors in western Kenya has increased AIDS-related deaths among teenage girls.
- Kisumu opposition FORD-Kenya Parliamentarian Peter Anyang' Nyong'o announces his defection from the party, saying he will only remain a "technical member" until parliament is dissolved.

- A vicious battle for survival is taking place at police headquartes leaving the country's top cops with little time to concentrate on their job at the height of escalating crime. ($1=56 Kenyan shillings)
